title: Initial omnific models of discrete initial surreal groups
description: Discrete initial additive groups of surreal numbers admit isomorphic initial models inside the omnific integers, including proper classes.
abstract: Every discrete initial ordered additive subgroup of the surreal numbers is order-group-isomorphic to a subgroup of the omnific integers that is initial in the surreal numbers. This holds for sets and proper classes in NBG with global choice and answers the discrete-group question posed by Kaplan and Ehrlich. An explicit operation on ordinal-length sign sequences moves the least exponent to zero without creating a right-simplicity-predecessor obligation. Relabeling the actual normal-form supports and normalizing only the bottom coefficient group then gives the required image. An appendix supplies a detailed sufficiency proof of the initial-group characterization used in the argument, addressing support exhaustion and the legality of limit-cut options.
plain_language: The surreal numbers contain familiar real numbers alongside infinite and infinitesimal quantities. They also have a construction tree: a number is simpler than another when its sign sequence is a shorter initial part of the other’s sequence. An initial group includes every such simpler predecessor of each of its elements.

This paper considers additive groups in that tree that have a smallest positive element. It gives each one an equivalent copy inside the omnific integers, while keeping the copy initial. The equivalence preserves addition and numerical order; it need not preserve where individual elements sit in the original construction tree.

The construction changes the exponents in the group’s existing normal forms and rescales only the lowest coefficient group. It works with the elements actually present, including groups that are proper classes, without adding a full group of all possible series.
result: In NBG set theory with global choice, every discrete initial ordered additive subgroup G of No is order-group-isomorphic to a subgroup H of the omnific integers Oz that is initial in No. Both sets and proper classes are included; the zero group is handled separately by the identity map. No closure under multiplication is assumed.

For a nonzero group, the least exponent is m=−α for a set ordinal α, and the coefficient group there is 2⁻ⁿℤ for some nonnegative integer n. The map sends m to zero, relabels all actual exponents by a strictly increasing sign-sequence operation, and multiplies the bottom coefficients by 2ⁿ. Its image has integral coefficient group ℤ at exponent zero and nonnegative exponents throughout.

The result answers the discrete additive-group question as posed in Kaplan’s 2015 thesis, the 2016 Oberwolfach contribution with Ehrlich, and Question 9.1 of the inspected Ehrlich–Kaplan author manuscript. Initiality means closure under simpler predecessors, rather than convexity in numerical order.
why_it_works: The exponent map preserves an initial image and reflects right-simplicity-predecessor relations. This prevents a new requirement for dyadic coefficients at the bottom, where the target coefficient group is ℤ.

Positive coefficient scaling and increasing exponent relabeling preserve addition and order. The image uses precisely the source supports, so truncation closure and the pure coefficient groups can be tracked exactly. The Ehrlich–Kaplan initial-group characterization then supplies initiality, and the usual normal-form criterion puts the image inside Oz.

The appendix provides a detailed sufficiency argument for the credited characterization. It first handles finite-support terms, then actual limit-length supports using legal integer perturbations, and reduces the proper-class case to set-sized initial exponent restrictions. Every individual surreal retains a set-sized support.
limitations: The hypothesis that G is an initial discrete ordered additive subgroup of No is essential to the stated result. This is not a classification of arbitrary abstract ordered groups or arbitrary noninitial surreal subgroups.

The isomorphism is required to preserve addition and numerical order, not simplicity or multiplication. The theorem does not say that the original G already lies in Oz, nor that its image is all of Oz.

The set-theoretic setting is NBG with global choice. Proper classes are allowed as groups and exponent classes; no proper-class support, class-sized sum or class-sized cut is used for an individual element.

The initial-group characterization, least-positive classification and general Hahn-group transport mechanisms are established prior work. The paper’s specific contribution is the exponent operation and its application to the actual subgroup, with the detailed dependency argument. No firstness or current worldwide-openness claim is made.

The finite verification programs are diagnostic checks. They do not prove the arbitrary-ordinal or proper-class statements; those depend on the written proof and its explicitly cited foundational surreal results.

background.title: Elliot Kaplan — Initial Embeddings in the Surreal Number Tree (2015)
background.note: The original discrete-group question appears in §7.1, Question 1, printed p. 47.

background.title: Kaplan, joint work with Ehrlich — Number systems with simplicity hierarchies (2016)
background.note: The published Oberwolfach contribution states the additive-group question at p. 3356 and distinguishes it from the established subdomain result.

background.title: Ehrlich and Kaplan — Number systems with simplicity hierarchies II
background.note: The inspected author manuscript supplies the canonical normal-form correspondence, initial-group characterization, coefficient and omnific criteria, and Question 9.1. Its related journal publication is JSL 83 (2018); the publisher body was not authenticated here.

background.title: Aschenbrenner, van den Dries and van der Hoeven — The surreal numbers as a universal H-field
background.note: Lemma 3.2 in the inspected 2016 version records the negative-ordinal minimum observation for an initial exponent set.

background.title: Kaplan, Krapp and Serra — Decomposing the automorphism group of the surreal numbers
background.note: Proposition 3.9 and Construction 3.10 give an explicit modern account of the established exponent-relabeling and positive coefficient-scaling mechanisms. They do not by themselves supply the initial-image conclusion here.
